_comment: Venue profiles used by aggregate_scores.py --venue / --all-venues. 'emphasis' multiplies the paper-type weights (order: technical_rigor, clarity, novelty, significance, experimental_validation, reproducibility, ethics) and is renormalized; these multipliers are this skill's heuristics, not official venue weights. 'bar_offset' shifts the composite thresholds (positive = harder). 'scale.status' records how well the scale is verified: official | confirmed (verified by the skill maintainer against the current form) | secondary | assumed | unpublished. 'as_of' is the review cycle the information describes. Verify against the venue's current reviewer guidelines before relying on labels.

cvpr.name: CVPR

scale.note: 6-point rating scale (confirmed by the maintainer, 2026-10). Label wording follows the ICCV 2025 reports (6 Accept, 5 Weak Accept, 4 Borderline Accept, 3 Borderline Reject, 2 Weak Reject, 1 Reject); check the exact label text on the current form.

cvpr.focus: Clear technical novelty, strong controlled experiments on standard benchmarks, ablations, visual results; the final justification must be explicitly tied to the rating and explain any post-rebuttal change.
cvpr.rebuttal: One-page PDF in the CVPR template (check current rules on new results).

iccv.name: ICCV

scale.note: 6-point rating scale (confirmed by the maintainer, 2026-10). Labels from ICCV 2025 reports: 6 Accept, 5 Weak Accept, 4 Borderline Accept; labels 3-1 inferred by symmetry.

iccv.focus: Same bar as CVPR; irresponsible or LLM-generated reviews are penalized by the venue.

eccv.name: ECCV

scale.note: 6-point rating scale (confirmed by the maintainer, 2026-10). Label wording follows the CVF-style labels; check the exact label text on the current form.

eccv.focus: Judge the paper against its declared Contribution Type; not beating SOTA on an existing benchmark is not by itself grounds for rejection; failing to cite or beat an arXiv paper must not be the sole reason to reject.

neurips.name: NeurIPS

scale.note: Quality/Clarity/Significance/Originality on 1-4, Overall 1-6 with Borderline accept/reject, Confidence 1-5 (2025 form). The skill's internal scales follow this form.

neurips.focus: Technically sound, complete work; originality need not mean an entirely new method; honest limitations are rewarded; the paper checklist is a tool, not grounds for rejection.
neurips.rebuttal: OpenReview comments with character limits, then discussion.

iclr.name: ICLR

scale.note: Soundness/Presentation/Contribution 1-4 and Confidence 1-5 are long-standing. Overall rating reported as {0,2,4,6,8,10} for ICLR 2026; earlier cycles used {1,3,5,6,8,10}. Both are shown.

iclr.focus: Reviews and submissions are public; authors can revise the PDF during discussion, so distinguish fixable from fundamental issues.
iclr.rebuttal: Public OpenReview discussion with PDF revisions.

icml.name: ICML

scale.note: ICML 2025: Overall Recommendation 1-5. ICML 2026 reportedly moved to a 6-point scale (Weak Accept = 4, Weak Reject = 3); use the 1-6 internal score with those labels if targeting 2026.

icml.focus: Whether claims are supported by evidence comes first; every strength or weakness must be substantiated.

aaai.name: AAAI

scale.note: AAAI does not publish its rating scale. Reported criteria: clarity, technical/experimental soundness, novelty, relevance. Two-phase review: papers with sufficiently negative Phase-1 reviews can be rejected before author feedback.

aaai.focus: Broad AI audience; papers must survive Phase 1 on three reviews, so first-impression clarity and an obvious contribution matter.

acmmm.name: ACM Multimedia

scale.note: Rating scale not confirmed. Guidelines stress novelty, rigor, claims supported by evidence, code/data release, and multimedia scope: papers on a narrow single modality without contributing to the human use of multimedia may be out of scope.

acmmm.focus: Multimodal/multimedia relevance is a gate; distinguish minor camera-ready fixes from major flaws.
acmmm.rebuttal: Optional OpenReview rebuttal; must stay anonymous and cannot link to external material (code, videos).

tmlr.name: TMLR

scale.note: Two criteria answered Yes/No with explanation: (1) Are the claims supported by accurate, convincing and clear evidence? (most important) (2) Would some individuals in TMLR's audience be interested in the findings? (if unsure, assume yes). Papers meeting both are accepted even if the contribution is modest; lack of SOTA or perceived novelty is not grounds for rejection.

tmlr.focus: Correctness and clarity of claims over novelty; over-claiming is fixed by narrowing claims or adding evidence.
tmlr.rebuttal: Open discussion with revisions; Action Editor decides.

tpami.name: IEEE TPAMI

scale.note: IEEE Computer Society recommendation options: Accept / Minor Revision / Major Revision / Revise and Resubmit / Reject; a second major revision is generally not granted.

fields: Relation to prior work (incl. authors' conference version)
tpami.focus: Top-conference bar plus completeness and depth; extended conference versions need substantial new content; comprehensive comparisons and analysis.

tip.name: IEEE TIP

scale.note: Exact TIP recommendation menu not confirmed; IEEE-style options assumed (Accept / Minor Revision / Major Revision / Reject & Resubmit / Reject).

tip.focus: Image-processing scope; fair baselines and ablations that separate the contribution from architecture size, data and tuning; reproducibility.
